rewrites.comment: Apple verifies a Sign in with Apple domain by fetching this exact path (F-091). The file itself is published under a plain name, because the `ignore` list above drops every dotted path and a negation is not expressible there — serving it by rewrite keeps one dotfile from being the reason hosting starts publishing all of them.

Apple's return URL for Sign in with Apple on the Play and Amazon builds (F-091). Apple POSTs the identity token to a registered https URL, and requires that URL's domain to be verified by the rewrite above — which cloudfunctions.net cannot serve and Hosting can.

Login with Amazon's return URL (F-091). The old flow bounced Amazon's authorization code to the app on a custom scheme, which any installed Android app may claim; here the code is filed server-side and never reaches the device. Register this URL as an allowed return URL in the Login with Amazon security profile before shipping a build that sets EXPO_PUBLIC_AMAZON_REDIRECT_URI.
